messages:
Priya (CS): Hey team, opening a support escalation for AcmeCorp — they're seeing streaming responses cut off consistently after ~90s, clients are reconnecting and getting partial outputs. Customer says sometimes they get charged for the partial stream AND the resumed stream. Ticket #INC-4321.

Alex S.: ugh. do we have their request_id or sample logs? sounds like an idle/timeout + client reconnect race.

Priya (CS): attaching what we have from customer (redacted). They used the browser SDK + a custom proxy. Root request id: rq_0a1b2c. No individual event timestamps but their client shows `onmessage` stopped, then `onopen` fired again ~6s later.

Priya (CS): repro steps from customer:
1) Browser connects via proxy -> our /v1/stream endpoint
2) After ~90s, browser receives no more events, EventSource triggers `error` -> reconnect.
3) New connection receives rest of generation or sometimes restarts from top. Billing shows 2 token usages for same prompt in some cases.

Ben T.: a few quick possibilities:
- proxy (nginx/traefik/ALB) idle timeouts dropping connection (common at ~60s or 120s)
- Cloudflare / CDN fronting might buffer and tear down long-lived connections
- client-side EventSource implementation: some browsers treat certain TCP resets as fatal and will reconnect w/new request id
- server-side we do send SSE comment pings? we currently send a `:\n\n` comment every 30s for long streams by default but only on specific routes.

Kevin L.: running infra note: ALBs default idle_timeout is 60s unless configured. Cloudflare default 100s. If the proxy in front doesn't see traffic it closes the connection. comment pings must be more frequent than the smallest proxied idle timeout.

Mira P. (DevEx): from SDK side — EventSource will reconnect automatically but it's a fresh request, so the server will treat it as a new generation and bill accordingly unless the client includes a resume token. We don't currently support automatic resume of partial generations for streaming.

Alex S.: suggestion: 1) ask customer to enable comment pings on their proxy path (every 15-25s), 2) set ALB/proxy idle timeout > client reconnect interval OR send pings faster than idle timeout. Also need to evaluate billing: if a request is interrupted server-side (we stopped producing) we probably recorded usage for tokens already produced. Resume would produce additional tokens. We can offer a credit but long-term we should detect reconnect-resume pairs using a `client_request_id` header.

Priya (CS): customer wants a safe short-term fix and a root cause. They run a custom nginx -> Cloudflare setup. They asked how to configure the comment ping server-side if they're using our hosted API (can't change our runtime).

Ben T.: for hosted API customers we can recommend these mitigations (short-term):
- Have client send a lightweight HTTP/1.1 keepalive to their proxy (but many proxies won't treat it as activity for idle timers).
- Use an application-level SSE comment ping: our runtime responds with SSE comments when the model hasn't produced tokens for X seconds. Example server-side comment ping (for reference):

```
# pseudo: send SSE comment ping every 20s
while streaming:
  if no_output_for(20s):
    # a comment line keeps proxies from idling
    send(':\n\n')
    flush()
```

This keeps ALB/Cloudflare from closing idle connection. But for hosted customers, they need to ensure their upstream (their proxy) doesn't buffer or strip comments.

Kevin L.: additional infra notes:
- If they have Cloudflare in front, make sure the route is configured as a `WebSocket`/long-poll-compatible or bypass Cloudflare's caching for that path. Cloudflare can buffer and drop long SSEs.
- ALB -> target group idle timeout must be >= 120s or set comment ping < 60s.

Mira P. (DevEx): long-term product asks:
- Add a `Client-Request-Id` header we encourage clients to set. On reconnect, clients re-send the same id and the runtime can dedupe or offer resume semantics (server chooses to resume or mark as duplicate).
- Add explicit `stream-resume` token in API so SDKs can try an idempotent resume path.

Alex S.: here's a quick repro script customers can run to confirm it's a proxy timeout vs runtime:

```
# simple SSE consumer to show keepalive/test
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-xx&prompt=long" > out.txt
# leave open, wait >90s. if connection drops but server log shows no error, likely proxy timeout.
```

And a minimal Node EventSource test:

```
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?...');
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = (err) => console.error('err', err);
```

Ben T.: about billing: ops-bot, can you lookup usage for rq_0a1b2c between 2026-03-10T10:00 and 2026-03-10T10:10? Customer claims double-charge.

ops-bot: Lookup initiated for request_id rq_0a1b2c. Aggregating usage... (this is an automated note).

ops-bot: Found two distinct token charge events for rq_0a1b2c: 432 tokens at 10:01 UTC, 210 tokens at 10:02 UTC. Possible explanation: first stream partially delivered then client reconnected and re-requested generation (new billed gen).

Priya (CS): I informed customer we can issue a goodwill credit for the second event while we investigate. They've accepted.

Kevin L.: action items for infra/eng:
- eng-runtime (Ben/Alex): confirm we emit SSE comment pings on hosted streams and verify they're not being stripped by any internal CDN. Consider reducing default ping interval to 20s for high-risk routes.
- eng-sre (Kevin): check ALB and proxy configs for long-lived connections; document recommended timeouts and add a KB article.
- devex (Mira): add `Client-Request-Id` header guidance and example in SDKs. Also add sample docs for user-side proxies (Cloudflare, ALB, nginx) with concrete config snippets.

Mira P. (DevEx): sample nginx proxy snippet to preserve SSE (recommendation):
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_read_timeout 180s; # make sure > expected duration
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```

Alex S.: I'll follow up with a small runtime change proposal: enable comment pings by default on all streaming endpoints with 20s interval and add a server-side `X-Stream-Heartbeat: 20` header so proxies/clients can detect. Will open PR and link here.

Priya (CS): Thanks all — customer credited, PR and KB article requested. I'll post a short status update to the customer once Alex opens the PR.

Ben T.: one more note: TCP keepalive at OS level is useful but often configured at >2h defaults. don't rely on TCP keepalive for short idle detection. application pings (SSE comments) are the reliable path. :thumbsup:

Priya (CS): closing loop for now. If anyone wants to add logs or follow-ups, please append here.
